## Verdict

## Bearer

MainRacePageViewModel — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/MainRacePageViewModel.kt

## Trigger

A power-save refresh tick, driven by AlwaysOnDisplayController entering
DisplayMode.POWER_SAVE (app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/display/AlwaysOnDisplayController.kt)
— nothing observed. `computeState()` never receives or consults the
current DisplayMode.

## Today

`SensorFreshnessWindow.WINDOW_MS` is 10_000ms
(core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/sensor/Freshness.kt),
and `AlwaysOnDisplayController.refreshIntervalMs` returns that same
value while `mode == DisplayMode.POWER_SAVE`
(app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/display/AlwaysOnDisplayController.kt),
so every power-save refresh lands a reading exactly at the freshness
window's edge. `MainRacePageViewModel.computeState()` evaluates
freshness the same way regardless of display mode: pace uses
`(lastKnownNow - at) <= SensorFreshnessWindow.WINDOW_MS` (line 172) and
falls back to `null` (rendered as a dash) when false or absent; heart
rate uses `SensorFreshnessWindow.evaluate` (lines 238-239) and falls
back to `null to null` when the result is not `Freshness.Fresh` (line
241). Neither `computeState()` nor its caller takes a `DisplayMode`
parameter, and `MainRacePageUiState` carries no field distinguishing a
normal fresh value from a power-save value that should stay shown and
dimmed. Which of §1.3's dash and §9.16's "stays shown, dimmed" applies
at the boundary follows only from Kotlin's `<=` in the freshness
comparisons the ViewModel happens to use, not from the display mode.

## Expected

`MainRacePageViewModel` receives the current `DisplayMode` (from
`AlwaysOnDisplayController`, already read by `MainActivity.kt`) and
`computeState()` consults it before applying a fallback: in
`DisplayMode.POWER_SAVE`, a value whose freshness evaluation is
`Freshness.Stale` (or, for pace, past the window) keeps rendering its
last known value, marked as dimmed, instead of falling back to a dash
or to `null`; in `DisplayMode.NORMAL` the existing dash/`null` fallback
is unchanged. This requires a second gap: `MainRacePageUiState` (and
`RaceCenterBlock.Pace`'s `paceText`, and the heart-rate/zone fields)
carry no representation of "shown but dimmed" distinct from a fresh
value or an absent one — that representation does not exist anywhere
in app-wear and must be added for the fallback to be rendered.
